curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8865-1/ (scans; the test car is pages 1-24, the alternate jeep after, and the 8720 motor add-on at the end)

functions.does: The steering wheel on the left steers the front wheels: its column, through two universal joints and a row of three 16-tooth gears, turns the 8-tooth pinion on the rack behind the front axle, and the rack's two links push the tall steering arms.
functions.source: book: cover (blueprint); steps 10 (rack and links), 13-14 (pinion shafts), 15 (steering arms), 23 (steering wheel)

functions.does: Pushing the car along turns the V4 engine: the rear wheels drive the differential, whose 14-tooth bevel pinion turns, through a row of three 8-tooth gears, the gearbox's layshaft, and through the gearbox the crankshaft, so the four pistons go up and down in the cylinder block and the flywheel at the back spins.
functions.source: book: cover (blueprint arrow at the back); steps 6-7 (differential, pinion and 8-tooth gears), 14 (gearbox), 18 (engine, pages 16-17)
functions.note: Kinebrick today: works. A turn of a rear wheel rolls the car one tyre round and turns the crankshaft 4/3 of a turn, each piston going through its 28 LDU stroke (tests/sets/8865-test-car.test.ts). The crankshaft's middle 24-tooth gear is held only by the two crank pins, on opposite sides of the main axle, so the webs either side of it are tied to turn together. The front wheels are 9 LDU above the ground, so the car stands on its rear wheels.

functions.does: The blue-knobbed gear lever between the seats picks one of three speeds: moving it fore and aft slides the gearbox's selector shaft, changing which of its 16- and 24-tooth gears mesh with the engine's and the layshaft's gears.
functions.source: book: step 14 (selector shaft, universal joint and blue knob), step 18 diagrams on page 17 (lever in positions 1, 2 and 3)
functions.note: Kinebrick today: doesn't. The lever turns round the selector shaft instead of sliding it, and the shaft can't slide. The probe needs a push along the car for this control (about 20 LDU between positions?), not a turn. Which position is first gear, and how far apart are the three positions?

functions.does: The differential lets the rear wheels turn at different speeds in a bend: with the engine held, turning one rear wheel turns the other the opposite way.
functions.source: book: step 6 (differential); inferred: what it's for
functions.note: Kinebrick today: partly, as checked, since the check holds nothing: the car stands on its rear wheels alone (the front ones are 9 LDU above the ground), and the drag rolls it along, turning the engine, rather than turning the other wheel the opposite way. With the engine held (frozen in the viewer), it works: turning one rear wheel turns the other the opposite way, the car standing on the ground (tests/bevel.test.ts).

functions.does: The front wheels have independent suspension: each rides on two grey suspension arms, upper and lower, with a shock absorber, and moves up and down.
functions.source: book: cover (blueprint arrow on the front wheel); steps 2, 9, 15-16
functions.note: Kinebrick today: doesn't. Swinging a lower arm turns only its pivot axle; the steering arm and wheel don't follow, and the shock absorbers spin on their pins rather than shortening.

functions.does: The rear wheels have independent suspension: each rides on an upright held between two wishbones of 1x6 bricks, with a shock absorber, and moves up and down, the half shafts' universal joints letting it.
functions.source: book: cover (blueprint arrow on the rear wheel); steps 1, 11-13 (wishbones, uprights and shock absorbers)
functions.note: Kinebrick today: doesn't. Swinging a wishbone turns only its pivot axle; the upright and wheel don't follow (the upright p361 flops on the lower wishbone's outer axle).

functions.does: The shock absorbers' springs hold the car up and spring back.
functions.skip: springs only matter under gravity or force

functions.does: The 16-tooth gear outside the left seat slides that seat fore and aft: its axle's 8-tooth pinion runs on a rack between the seat's two rails.
functions.source: book: cover (blueprint arrows under the seat); steps 10 (rails and racks), 12 (pinion blocks), 23 (seats)
functions.note: Kinebrick today: doesn't. The seat is held as turning on one rail rather than sliding along both, so the gear is locked.

functions.does: The 16-tooth gear outside the right seat slides that seat fore and aft, as on the left.
functions.note: Kinebrick today: doesn't, as the left seat.

functions.does: Each seat's backrest reclines on its hinge plates, and the headrest tilts on its own hinge.
functions.source: book: cover (curved blueprint arrow at the seat back); step 23 (seat assembly with hinges)
functions.note: Kinebrick today: doesn't; each seat is one rigid body. Friction hinges: whether this belongs here or under skip is for the owner to say.

functions.does: The red-knobbed lever left of the gear lever raises the pop-up headlights: it turns a long shaft that runs forward under the car through a universal joint to a crank at the front, which, through a short link and crossbar, turns the two headlight axles so the round white headlights flip up.
functions.source: book: cover (curved blueprint arrow at the headlights); steps 5 (long shaft, universal joint and red knob), 17 (headlights); inferred: that the lever works the headlights, from the parts
functions.note: Kinebrick today: doesn't. The lever turns on its own pin without turning the shaft; the shaft (p114) is locked, and so are the headlights: the toothed half bushes lock the headlight pods and the crossbar's toggle joints to the headlight axles p471 and p472, so the pods turn with their axles, and the crossbar p125 holds the axles as still as the shaft. Is this really what the red lever does?

questions.question: Does the red lever raise the headlights? How far apart are the gear lever's three positions? Should the reclining seats be functions or `skip`?
